marker.description: Teal dot marking the temporal bone surface near the TMJ.

main_question: Identify the bony structure indicated by the teal marker.
main_answer: Mandibular fossa (Glenoid fossa) of the temporal bone
main_explanation: The marker is located on the temporal bone, specifically in the depression that articulates with the mandibular condyle, known as the mandibular or glenoid fossa.

supporting_question.question: Which nerve provides the primary sensory innervation to the temporomandibular joint?
supporting_question.explanation: The auriculotemporal nerve, a branch of the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve (V3), provides the main sensory supply to the TMJ.
